source: Category Guardrails for Local Performance Ads (Oct 29, 2026)
precedence: Every film runs the universal guardrails first, then its category rules. When a universal rule and a category rule conflict, the stricter rule wins. These sit on top of Product Spine v2 rules M1-M27; Claims extends M22.
regulatory_note: Regulatory notes are a working summary (ASCI Code, CPA 2019, CCPA guidelines 2022), not legal advice. Review quarterly with a legal check.
matching_notes: Terms are matched case-insensitively in Roman and Devanagari, with letter boundaries; nukta and Devanagari digits are normalised. 'regex' entries are JavaScript regular expressions applied to the normalised text (write Devanagari without nukta).

Real Estate & Home Decor.flag: This business type covers both property and decor. Property rules (RERA number required) apply until the owner says the film is about decor only.

Other Local Business.flag: No category module fits 'Other Local Business'. Only the universal rules apply until the owner picks a category.

Real Estate, Builder & Interior Designer.flag: Builders sell property (RERA rules); interior designers are decor. Property rules apply until the owner says the film is about decor only.

Skincare, Cosmetics & Wellness.flag: Selling skincare or cosmetics is not a salon service, and 'wellness' can mean healthcare. Not mapped automatically - the owner must pick the category.

Hardware, Electrical & Sanitaryware.flag: Hardware and sanitaryware fit neither Electronics & Gadgets nor Decor cleanly. Not mapped automatically - the owner must pick the category.

Footwear, Bags & Leather Goods.flag: Footwear and bags are not named in the Fashion & Apparel module. Not mapped automatically - the owner must pick the category.

Optical, Eyewear & Sunglasses.flag: Eye tests are health services but eyewear retail is not. Not mapped automatically - the owner must pick the category.

Gifts, Toys, Books & Stationery.flag: No category module covers gifts, toys, books or stationery. Only the universal rules apply.

Photography, Events & Wedding Services.flag: No category module covers photography or events. Only the universal rules apply.

Dry Fruits, Organic & Gourmet Food.flag: Dry-fruit and gourmet retail is food but not a sweet shop, bakery or restaurant. Not mapped automatically - the owner must pick the category.

Pet Care, Clinic & Pet Shop.flag: Veterinary care is not covered by the human Healthcare & Clinic module. Only the universal rules apply until the owner picks a category.

Professional, Legal & Business Services.flag: No category module covers professional or legal services. Only the universal rules apply.

Other.flag: No category module fits 'Other'. Only the universal rules apply until the owner picks a category.

rules.text: Every factual claim must trace to a form field. Never invent prices, discounts, stock levels, years in business, customer counts or awards.
No superlatives (best, No. 1, cheapest, lowest, most trusted, only) unless documented proof is uploaded.
No fake urgency ("only today", "last 2 pieces", countdowns, "stock khatam") unless the offer states a real end date (Dark Patterns guidelines 2023, CCPA).
State offers in full: "up to 50% off" must not imply everything is 50% off; "Free" only if nothing must be bought to get it.
No comparison with named or recognisable competitors, online platforms or brands. A generic "online se sasta" dig is allowed only if it is true.
No fake testimonials (M23): no acted "real customer" claims, no fake ratings, stars or review screenshots.
No celebrity, influencer or public-figure look-alikes, voices or names. No AI face that resembles a real person.
Never mock body type, skin colour, age, caste, religion, region, accent, disability or gender. No fairness-as-success.
No harmful gender stereotypes (a woman shown only as cook or cleaner who fails; a man mocked for doing housework).
Children: no unsafe act, no pester-power ("tell your papa to buy"), no child shown inferior for not owning something, no sexualised styling of minors.
No alcohol, tobacco, gutka or pan masala anywhere in frame, including the background.
No unsafe acts that could be copied: no riding without a helmet, no phone while driving, no open flames near gas, no kids near hot oil, no live wires.
No real currency notes in close-up being thrown or stepped on. No misuse of the national emblem or flag.
No deities, idols or religious symbols (M24). No political symbols, parties or leaders.
No legible text, logos, brand packaging or price tags in generated scenes (M8). Shelves are unbranded or blurred.
Avoid close-ups of fingers doing fine work (counting notes, threading needles, typing). Prefer medium shots.
Products are generic versions of what the owner sells - never a specific branded item the shop does not stock.
One location per scene and at most two speaking characters in the film, unless the Storytelling format needs three.
Use the owner's [PHOTOS] as reference. The generated shop must never look grander than the real one (M13).

Meta and YouTube reject before/after body images, "you" statements about personal attributes ("Are you fat?", "Struggling with debt?"), sensational health claims and misleading buttons. Hooks talk about a situation, not the viewer's body or condition.

visual_rules: Show a range of body types, ages and skin tones; never a "too fat to fit" gag.
No revealing or sexualised framing and no slow body-pans. Frame face-and-shoulders to full outfit at medium distance.
Trial rooms: never show undressing. Cut from the person entering to the person stepping out dressed.
Mannequins and racks look like a town boutique, not a mall.
ai_weaknesses: Patterns, embroidery and borders morph between frames: prefer solid colours or simple prints.
Keep the same garment reference across scenes.
Avoid zari close-ups across a cut.
human_truths: A mother adjusting her daughter's dupatta before a photo.
A college student hunting for one outfit that works for three events.
A blouse that must fit by the wedding.
hook_preferences: Everyday crisis (a button pops, a fitting goes wrong).
endings: The outfit worn in the moment it was bought for.
do: Owner-stated fabrics and offers, exactly as given.
Medium framing, one simple garment carried across scenes.
dont: Celebrity or film references, designer look-alikes or logos.
Fake MRP slashes.
Undressing, body-pans, "slim/fat" judgements, fairness language.
fashion.regulatory_notes: Silk Mark and Handloom Mark are certification marks; GI names (Banarasi, Kanjeevaram, Paithani, Chanderi) need the owner to confirm the source.

regex: (cancer|कैंसर|heart attack|हार्ट अटैक)\s*(ho sakta|हो सकता|हो सकती|can happen|could be)

auto_reject_visuals.label: Blood, needles entering skin, surgery or wounds
Patients in distress or sick children crying
Red cross symbol, medical council logo or certificates
Branded medicine boxes or handing medicine without prescription

visual_rules: No blood, needles entering skin, surgery, wounds, X-rays of real anatomy, or patients in distress.
Show a calm waiting area, a receptionist, a doctor listening.
No patient faces implied to be real patients; no sick children crying.
A white coat and stethoscope are fine; no medical council logo, red cross symbol or certificates.
Pharmacy: unbranded boxes; never hand over medicines without a prescription (except general items).
human_truths: Late-night fever and a shuttered market.
An elderly father who won't go "for small things".
A pharmacist explaining the dose slowly.
A mother holding her child's hand.
hook_preferences: Counter question ("भैया, ये दवाई कब लेनी है?").
Area shoutout ("[AREA] में रात को भी खुला है").
endings: Worry eased (a sleeping child, a father nodding).
dont: Outcomes, cures, guarantees, success rates, "best doctor".
Named medicines, testimonials, fear hooks.
Blood, needles, wounds, red cross.
healthcare.regulatory_notes: Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act 1954 (listed conditions include diabetes, cancer, obesity, sexual dysfunction, infertility and more). NMC rules restrict doctor self-promotion - the owner confirms compliance. Schedule H/H1/X drugs are not advertised. AYUSH: no "cure".
